items.title: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers
items.summary: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here.

items.title: A disproof of the El-Zahar--Erd\H{o}s conjecture
items.summary: El-Zahar and Erd\H{o}s asked whether every graph of bounded clique number and sufficiently large chromatic number contains two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs, each of large chromatic number, with no edge between them. We give a negative answer even for triangle-free graphs. For every integer $g \ge 4$, we show by a probabilistic argument that there exist graphs of girth at least $g$ and arbitrarily large chromatic number in which any two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs that each require at least seven colors are joined by an edge.

items.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem for number fields
items.summary: Given a quadratic number field $K$ we show that the $abc$ conjecture over $K$ implies that $\mathbb{Z}$ is Diophantine in $K$ and, hence, a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over $K$. More generally, the same conclusions hold for an arbitrary number field $K$ provided that the $abc$ conjecture holds over $K$ and that there is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose rank is positive and does not increase over $K$.

items.title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
items.summary: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos.

items.title: Black hole binary mergers in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity with regularisation
items.summary: We study the non-linear dynamics of Chern-Simons gravity with numerical relativity for the first time. We use the regularisation prescription to obtain a well-posed initial-value formulation in the gauges commonly used in numerical relativity, and we simulate head-on collisions and binary black hole mergers in the regime of validity of effective field theory, extracting the corresponding scalar and gravitational waves. This opens up the possibility to test general effective field theories of gravity, including those with higher-than-second-order equations of motion, with gravitational waves.

items.title: Oscillatory integral operators of arbitrary signature: beyond the universal estimates
items.summary: We consider H\"ormander oscillatory integral operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. In particular, we are interested in proving bounds with dependence on the signature of the phase. The sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^p$ estimates was obtained for any given signature by the second author and Iliopoulou. Under the mild non-compression hypotheses on the phase introduced in Chen et al., we prove $L^p\to L^p$ estimates that go beyond this universal range in odd dimensions. We also obtain the sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^q$ estimates for odd $n$. The techniques are based on the breakthrough work of Wang--Wu on the Fourier restriction conjecture.

items.title: Periods, isomonodromy, and modularity of ALG/ALG$^*$ gravitational instantons

We compute the compact hyperk\"ahler periods and asymptotic parameters of these moduli spaces and give explicit inverse formulas for every admissible choice of these data. For the three ALG types, global isomonodromic transport realizes the two real parameters left undetermined by the compact periods. We use a Hamiltonian variation formula and uniform comparison with the semiflat metric to apply the Torelli and uniqueness theorems.

Within this framework, we revisit the derivation of these metrics using the Kerr--Schild approach for illustrative purposes. The Maxwell equations are solved independently of the Kerr--Schild function, allowing the electromagnetic source to be determined before addressing the gravitational field equations. items.title: Orbit-averaged spinning and eccentric binary black holes: Hamiltonian and integrability
items.summary: For over two decades, the orbit-averaged precession equations of spinning binary black holes at second post-Newtonian order have been a standard model for their spin dynamics. One of their constants of motion, the projected effective spin, underlies the stability analysis of aligned-spin configurations and the construction of analytical solutions. The system is known to be Hamiltonian and integrable, its Hamiltonian being the orbit average of the full post-Newtonian Hamiltonian. Independently, we derive this Hamiltonian from the equations of motion alone, show why the orbit average gives the correct equations, and relate its constants of motion to those of the full system. items.title: Search for Heavy Charged Higgs Bosons in Boosted Top and Bottom Quark Final States at a 1.4 TeV Future Lepton Collider
items.summary: The discovery potential for heavy charged Higgs bosons $H^\pm$ decaying into a top-bottom quark pair is investigated at a future $e^+e^-$ collider operating at $\sqrt{s}=1.4~\mathrm{TeV}$. The study considers charged Higgs masses between 200 and 600 GeV within all four Yukawa types of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM). The boosted $tb$ final state is explored using complementary cut-based and machine-learning analyses based on boosted decision trees (BDT). The expected signal significance and sensitivity contours in the $(m_{H^\pm},\tan\beta)$ plane are obtained for each Yukawa type. The resulting sensitivity extends to regions of the 2HDM parameter space beyond the projected reach of the…

items.title: An $\infty$-category approach to $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories
items.summary: $A_\infty$-algebras over a commutative ring $R$ are generalizations of $R$-algebras in which multiplication is only associative up to higher homotopies. Similarly, $A_\infty$-categories over $R$ are generalizations of $R$-linear categories in which composition of morphisms is only associative up to higher homotopies. They are important in the definition of Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry, and in other areas of mathematics. By $\infty$-categories we mean quasicategories, a class of simplicial sets which are a model for $(\infty,1)$-categories, used in the work of Jacob Lurie. We define and study $\infty$-categories of $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories. Our approach is…

items.summary: Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. items.title: Testing the Universality of RAR Model with Constraints on Fermionic Dark Matter for M31
items.summary: The Ruffini--Arg\"uelles--Rueda (RAR) model describes dark matter as a self-gravitating system of massive fermions in thermodynamic equilibrium within general relativity. It suggests a dual morphology in galaxies: a highly degenerate quantum core mimicking a central supermassive black hole, and a classical halo that explains galactic rotation curves. Earlier applications of the model to the Milky Way restricted the fermion mass to $mc^{2}=48\text{--}345~\text{keV}$, and the orbits of the S-stars around Sagittarius~A$^{\ast}$ (Sgr~A$^{\ast}$) favored $mc^{2}=56~\text{keV}$, whereas a recent thermodynamic stability analysis allows only $mc^{2}\approx194\text{--}387~\text{keV}$. items.title: Thermal Resummation Effects on Electroweak Phase Transitions and Gravitational Waves in Conformal and Non-Conformal 2HDMs
items.summary: We quantify how thermal resummation affects electroweak phase transitions and gravitational-wave predictions in classically conformal and non-conformal two-Higgs-doublet models. We compare multi-field partial dressing (PD), which retains the full thermal functions and determines scalar masses and mixing from gap equations, with the Parwani and Arnold-Espinosa (AE) prescriptions at identical zero-temperature inputs. Completed first-order transitions dominate the conformal scan under all three prescriptions. items.title: Quiver-Invariant Triality between Brane Brick Models
items.summary: We study quiver-invariant triality between 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories described by brane brick models associated with toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds. The dual theories share the same gauge groups, field content and E-terms but have distinct J-terms. We present an explicit pair of such brane brick models and identify the sequence of triality mutations relating them. This sequence returns the quiver to its original form while transforming the J- and E-terms. We explain the relation between quiver-invariant triality and the orbifold reduction of quiver-invariant brane tilings.

items.title: The BSM Rollercoaster, 1980-2000
items.summary: This contribution is a personal historical retrospective on beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) physics from 1978 to the early 2000s, organized around its emotional rollercoaster. I trace two waves of optimism separated by a multiyear contraction of confidence, both ultimately ending in disappointment when decisive experimental confirmation failed to arrive. The story begins in 1978, when the Standard Model emerged as the front-runner. It then moves from the first wave of excitement over naturalness and Technicolor, rumored proton-decay events, and the construction of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, to the contraction of confidence in the late 1980s. items.title: Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications: From Circles to Strings
items.summary: This review is written with a simple question in mind: what does one need to know to enter the literature on Scherk-Schwarz compactifications? It is organized as a sequence of questions that a graduate student might naturally ask, together with the concepts, calculations, and formal tools needed to work through the literature. The discussion starts at an elementary field-theory level and gradually develops toward more advanced aspects of supergravity, orbifolds, quantum effects, and string theory. Phenomenological applications are deliberately left aside.

items.title: Accretion disks and photon rings in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
items.summary: We investigate thin accretion disks and photon rings around a static black hole in Palatini Kalb Ramond gravity, connecting thermal emission with the optical effects of the radial geometry. items.summary: The effective field theory approach constructs the low-energy theory by integrating out fluctuations above an ultraviolet scale which raises the cosmological constant and hierarchy problems. We investigate an alternative prescription in which the quantum theory is restricted to a finite accessible region of phase space, characterized by a dimensionless cardinality $\mathcal N$, rather than by independently prescribed spacetime and momentum scales. items.title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
items.summary: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. items.title: A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties
items.summary: We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. items.title: Supersymmetric Hilbert complexes and Witten deformation on stratified pseudomanifolds
items.summary: We present a framework to study topics related to index theory and Dirac operators with N=1,2 supersymmetry (SUSY), extending it to stratified pseudomanifolds with wedge metrics (iterated conic metrics). items.summary: Can a Euclidean axion wormhole extend to infinity with every instanton still suppressed? The imaginary distance bound says it cannot: some instanton must become actionless first. items.title: Algebraic matroids with non-algebraic duals exist in any positive characteristic
items.summary: We show that for every field $K$ of positive characteristic there exists an algebraic matroid $M$ over $K$ such that the dual matroid $M^*$ is not algebraic over any field. Our conceptual proof relies on the theory of matroids over one-dimensional algebraic groups. As an application, we deduce that the classes of supports of realizable volume polynomials and of realizable covolume polynomials differ in positive characteristic.

items.title: Partial flags of tropical linear spaces may not complete
items.summary: We construct two valuated matroids of ranks 2 and 4 on eight elements that form a valuated quotient, such that no rank 3 valuated matroid forms a valuated quotient with both simultaneously. In other words, a partial flag of tropical linear spaces need not extend to a complete flag containing every intermediate dimension.

items.title: Strong Coupling of Cosmological Perturbations in mLQC-I: The Hybrid Approach
items.summary: We study nonlinear perturbative consistency of scalar perturbations in modified loop quantum cosmology I (mLQC-I) within the hybrid approach. We express the quadratic and cubic Hamiltonians in a common canonical representation before imposing the background constraint and adopt a minimal sector-preserving cubic regularization. Near the pre-bounce quantum-geometrical de Sitter phase, nonlinear coefficients become strongly enhanced. The $\alpha_I^3/\kappa$ term survives the leading ultraviolet cubic kernel for fixed nondegenerate triangles in the selected frequency assignment. items.title: Global well-posedness for the 2D full compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system
items.summary: This paper establishes the global well-posedness and nonlinear stability of the 2D full compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system $\mathbb T^2$, for smooth initial data close to the equilibrium with constant density and temperature, zero velocity and background magnetic field $\mathbf e_2=(0,1)$. Neither the density nor the magnetic field is damped or diffused in this system. Here, we impose no Diophantine condition on the background magnetic field, no symmetry on the data and no special geometry on the domain. items.title: Photon-Mediated Axino-Bino Scattering Process for the LZ High-Energy Recoil Event
items.summary: We for the first time investigate the photon-mediated endothermic axino-bino scattering process to explain the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy recoil event. We calculate the signals from non-relativistic halo and boosted dark matter (DM), including natural xenon isotopes, detector efficiency, and energy resolution. For a fixed Standard Halo Model (SHM) distribution, a simplified three-bin Poisson analysis yields a best-fit benchmark with mass $m\simeq506\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and mass splitting $\delta\simeq326\,\mathrm{keV}$ at the adopted upper coupling bound $g_\gamma=10^{-3}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. items.title: Twist and Shout: defect lines on the R\'enyi torus
items.summary: We consider what the entanglement between two regions of a critical system can reveal about its symmetries, including non-invertible ones. For two intervals in a two-dimensional conformal field theory, the second R\'enyi entropy is a partition function on a torus, and a topological defect line can be wrapped around one of the intervals. For an on-site symmetry this computes the overlap of the reduced density matrix with its image under the symmetry acting on one interval, and in general it defines an observable that depends only on the cross-ratio. items.title: Quantum Autoencoder on Real Hardware for New Physics Searches at Muon Colliders
items.summary: We apply a quantum autoencoder to search for new physics (NP) in the tri-photon process $\mu^+\mu^-\to\gamma\gamma\gamma$ at muon colliders. Using a six-qubit circuit on the Tianyan176 quantum computer, we measure the reconstruction losses for Standard Model (SM) events and anomalous quartic gauge couplings (aQGCs) events. The results demonstrate that the hardware-implemented quantum autoencoder effectively discriminates NP signals from the SM background. Concurrently, we derive the expected constraints on the aQGCs coefficients and compare them with those obtained from conventional methods.

items.title: Parity restoration in a sterile-neutrino scenario: bounds from atomic parity violation to the LHC
items.summary: In a four-fermion-interaction scenario beyond the Standard Model (SM), in which right-handed (sterile) neutrinos take part in TeV-scale composite dynamics, the $Z$ boson acquires an energy-dependent right-handed coupling $\GR(q^2)$ that is expected to vanish at low energies and to restore parity symmetry at high energies. items.title: The Universality of Halo Growth and Merger Rates in Modified Gravity Theories
items.summary: In the standard $\Lambda$CDM framework, the merger rate of dark matter haloes has been found to follow a nearly universal form, with only weak dependence on halo mass and redshift. We examine whether this universality is preserved in modified gravity (MG) models, where the growth of cosmic structure can deviate from that of general relativity (GR). We use the ELEPHANT suite of large $N$-body simulations to study halo merger rates and mass accretion histories in different modified gravity models, including two representative scenarios beyond-GR: the Hu--Sawicki chameleon $f(R)$ model and the normal branch of the Dvali--Gabadadze--Porrati model. items.title: Gamma-Ray Bursts from Primordial Black Hole-Induced Neutron Star Collapse
items.summary: We show that the capture and subsequent endoparasitic consumption of a neutron star (NS) by a primordial black hole (PBH) can produce a short gamma-ray burst (GRB) without forming an accretion disk. During PBH-induced NS consumption, the NS spin is amplified through angular-momentum conservation and transfer from infalling matter, while flux freezing and a differential-rotation-driven dynamo amplify the magnetic field. We find that, for rapidly rotating millisecond pulsars (MSPs), these mechanisms can power short GRBs through magnetic dipole radiation and magnetic energy release. If asteroid-mass PBHs in the range $10^{-14}M_\odot$--$10^{-11}M_\odot$ constitute the dark matter, we estimate…

items.title: From Instantons to AdS Boundaries: Tracing the Geometric Path from Quantum Anomalies to Massive Gravity
items.summary: This thesis studies how boundary data enter two gravitational observables: the Dirac index on gravitational instantons and conserved charges in three-dimensional New Massive Gravity. In Einstein gravity coupled to ModMax electrodynamics, we compute the index of charged Dirac fermions on Taub-NUT and Eguchi-Hanson instantons using the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer theorem, which includes the spectral asymmetry of the boundary Dirac operator. The Taub-NUT index agrees with the Maxwell result. items.title: Exceptional zeros for $\mathrm{GSp}(4) \times \mathrm{GL}(2)$ and Yoshida lifts
items.summary: The aim of this article is to study an exceptional zero phenomenon for the $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $\mathrm{GSp}_4\times\mathrm{GL}_2$ in the critical regions (F) and (D). We construct improved $p$-adic $L$-functions by replacing the $p$-depleted Eisenstein family with its $p$-ordinary counterpart. Under a local compatibility hypothesis at the ramified places and classical control for the families, we show that their poles detect exactly the Yoshida lifts whose smaller constituent is dual to the $\mathrm{GL}_2$ representation. items.title: First $\Omega_{\rm m}-w$ Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
items.summary: Though fast radio bursts (FRBs) are widely advocated as a dark energy probe, no valid $\Omega_m-w$ constraint has been obtained exclusively from FRB data to date. Benefiting from a rapidly growing localized sample and a novel statistical framework for modeling the dispersion measure (DM), we report the first simultaneous inference of the matter density $\Omega_m$ and dark energy equation of state parameter $w$ from FRBs alone, without external observational priors on these two parameters. We combine a multi-parameter emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum with a physically motivated electron prescription to construct a cosmology-dependent cosmic-DM distribution. items.summary: We develop a simple analytic two-component model that links the thermal evolution of self-gravitating systems to black-hole thermodynamics. The model consists of a monatomic nonrelativistic ideal gas and an effective barotropic support calibrated by the specific heat $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(\Theta)$ of a J\"uttner gas. items.title: Star-forming disc galaxies align tangentially with the cosmic tidal field
items.summary: The alignments of galaxy shapes, with one another and with the large-scale structure of the Universe, have been a topic of considerable investigation within cosmology and extragalactic astrophysics for the last 60 years. Galaxy alignments are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and help us learn about the processes of galaxy formation. Red early-type galaxies are known to show strong radial alignments around other galaxies; however, blue star-forming galaxies have shown little evidence of alignment. We combine SPHEREx spectrophotometry with DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys to build a full-sky catalogue of 71 million galaxies with precise redshifts. With this catalogue we are able…

items.title: $C_T$ and $C_J$ of general scalar--fermion conformal field theories in $d=4-\epsilon$
items.summary: We compute $C_T$ and $C_J$, the coefficients of the stress-tensor and conserved-current two-point functions, to order $\epsilon^3$ at any fixed point of the general renormalizable theory of scalars and fermions in $d=4-\epsilon$. We give explicit results for the chiral Ising, XY and Heisenberg models and for fixed points with emergent supersymmetry in $d=3$. items.title: Algebraic independence of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms via period interpretations
items.summary: Based on Hartl's de Rham-crystalline comparison isomorphism, we formulate a notion of Andr\'{e}'s $v$-adic periods for a class of Anderson $\mathbb{F}_q[z]$-motives with respect to a degree-one finite place $v$ of a rational function field over a finite field, following Ancona-Fr\u{a}\c{t}il\u{a}'s formulation of $p$-adic periods. items.summary: We consider orbifolds of 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory that preserve minimal supersymmetry and study their conformal manifolds, focusing on two families of Abelian orbifolds in the planar limit. We compute their superconformal indices, construct their complete single-trace BPS spectra and identify the conformal manifolds. These are generically spanned by a subset of the gauge-couplings, whose number we derive from both gauge and string theory, and a universal Leigh--Strassler-type superpotential deformation. items.summary: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) have found evidence for a gravitational wave background at nHz frequencies. Inspiralling supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs) likely contribute to at least part of the signal, but there may be additional cosmological sources from new physics in the early universe. Disentangling the two is complicated by the prohibitively slow modelling of SMBHB spectra based on realistic population models. items.summary: For the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^2$, we prove that vertical viscosity alone yields global $H^2$ stability and algebraic decay of the vorticity and velocity for small reflection-symmetric data with polynomially weighted vorticity. Under stronger smallness assumptions, we obtain $H^3$ stability and vorticity-gradient decay, in contrast to unbounded gradient growth for Euler flows in the same symmetry class. items.summary: We study the stabilization of the three complex moduli associated with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ modular symmetry by gaugino condensation in $\mathcal N=1$ supergravity models from heterotic string theory, where one-loop threshold corrections fix both the modular weight and the singularity structure of the superpotential. items.summary: We study least energy fully non-trivial solutions of a nonlinear Schr\"odinger system with Sobolev critical nonlinearities and repulsive interaction involving all the components at the same time. Under the scalar Brezis-Nirenberg assumptions on the linear coefficients, we prove existence of least energy fully non-trivial solutions on smooth bounded domains for every negative coupling in dimensions \(N=5,6\). items.title: Cosmological First-Order Phase Transitions with Full Nonlinear Gravity
items.summary: Cosmological first-order phase transitions can contribute to the stochastic gravitational wave background. For decades, these first-order phase transitions have been studied using a Friedmann--Lema\^itre--Robertson--Walker background where the gravitational waves are treated as linear perturbations. Here, we present simulations of a first-order phase transition in the presence of fully nonlinear general relativity, using the BSSN formalism. We simulate a universe that contains a scalar field alongside a relativistic radiation fluid. We focus on GUT-scale transitions in which bubbles nucleate near the horizon size. items.title: On the local boundedness of weak solutions to doubly nonlinear equations with variable exponents
items.summary: We establish local boundedness, together with quantitative estimates, for non-negative weak sub-solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear parabolic equations whose prototype is \[ (u^q)_t-\operatorname{div} \Big(|Du|^{p(x,t)-2}Du\Big)=0, \qquad p(x,t)>1,\quad q>0. \] The results are obtained under a logarithmic continuity condition on the variable exponent $p(x,t)$ and suitable relations between $q$ and the local bounds of $p(x,t)$. In certain ranges of the exponents, an additional local integrability assumption is required.

items.title: Atomic MathReasoner: Instance-Level Composition of Atomic Reasoning Skills for Mathematical LLMs
items.summary: Most existing approaches enhance mathematical reasoning in large language models (LLMs) as a monolithic capability, despite the fact that different mathematical problems require different reasoning skills. Recent work has explored a more fine-grained perspective by decomposing mathematical reasoning into atomic skills and developing specialized modules for individual capabilities. However, how to effectively utilize these atomic abilities remains underexplored. To address this challenge, we propose Atomic MathReasoner (AMR), an instance-level framework for composing atomic reasoning skills. items.summary: The precise distribution of baryons in the Universe remains an open question in cosmology, as their highly diffuse nature hinders direct observation. We use fast radio bursts (FRBs) and their dispersion measures (DMs) to probe and localise this baryon distribution in the large-scale structure (LSS). items.summary: Redrock is a software package for spectroscopic classification and redshift fitting, designed to use the full information from spectroperfectionism outputs: flux-calibrated spectra, uncorrelated errors, and a per-spectrum resolution matrix encoding the non-Gaussian wavelength-dependent spectral line-spread function. items.title: Real Fr{\o}yshov invariants and lattice homology
items.summary: For a class of almost rational plumbing 4-manifolds equipped with smooth involutions, we give a description of the Real Fr{\o}yshov invariants of their boundaries in terms of lattice homology. items.summary: An isolating set of a hypergraph $H$ is a vertex set whose closed neighbourhood intersects every edge of $H$. The isolation number $\iota(H)$ is the minimum cardinality of such a set. items.summary: Extracting precise universal data on conformal field theory (CFT) on the lattice traditionally requires large-scale simulations of the ground states and excitations of critical systems.
